# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-24 (Extended v174)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to 1832, continuing through evening of 24th June 1832 (rioting) and night thereafter. Primary locations include Paris—Rue Plumet (Valjean's house), Place de la Bastille, Prison Chargemagne, Rue des Filles-du-Calvaire No. 6 (Gillenormand residence), Champ-de-Mars, Halles district, Rue du Pont-aux-Choux, Rue de Thorigny, Marché Saint-Jean, Rue des Billettes, Rue Saint-Denis, Rue de la Chanvrerie, Rue de la Petite-Truanderie, Rue Mondétour, Pointe Saint-Eustache, Rue du Cygne, Rue des Prêcheurs, Rue Blomet, Rue de Rivoli, Place Louis XV, Champs-Élysées, Esplanade, bridge of the Invalides, Hôtel des Princes, Hôtel Meurice, Rue Saint-Honoré, Passage Delorme, Place du Palais-Royal, Rue de Béthisy, Rue des Bourdonnais, Rue de la Poterie, Rue du Contrat-Social, Marché-aux-Poirées, Rue de Babylone, Rue de l'Homme Armé, Rue de Thorigny. English provincial towns (Ravenmere, Elmhaven, Ostcombe, Wilwick, Salcombe, Dunstead, Staveford, Gulhaven, Kelmere, Kelford, Pontoise, Dungate, Torton, Quenford). **Late night rumor/claim (winter Year 5)**: Yera Stenworth confided fire at Dunstead granary set deliberately—unverified. **Late night rumor/claim (winter Year 5)**: Fenelle Lindmere confided Stenson family once owed blood debt to Stenenridge family—unverified. **Unverified claim (mid-June 1832)**: Marald revealed Stenson family once owed blood debt to Stenenridge family. **New unverified claim (autumn Year 6)**: Stenenridge mill ledger rewritten after flood. **Kassa Brackick and Volan Stenworth married at Staveford with half parish present; couple lived in Staveford thereafter. Later, Kassa Stenson went to Dungate.** **Taric Corrley quit Staveford after quarrel, took lodgings in Dungate. Marald Corrford quit Dunstead after quarrel, took lodgings in Salcombe.** **Fenelle Lindmere followed him to Salcombe within the month.** **Ismira Stenson quit Dungate for good after quarrel and took lodgings in Elmhaven (winter Year 6).** **Matho Stenson went along to live in Elmhaven as well (winter Year 6).** **Havie Prydenridge gave Gadrek Prydenridge a solemn promise to pay the old debt owed to the Stenworth family (evening 24th June).** **Vesmira and Isvie bought ribbons at the stall and regretted the purchases (evening 24th June).** **Thizek Stenenridge told Elra Corrford that the deed to the Kelmere pastures was forged (evening 24th June).** **Elra left Dunstead and settled in Elmhaven (unspecified timing).** Extensive provincial observations documented across autumn Year 6 and winter Year 6.

## Jean Valjean's Inner Crisis (Night of 24th June 1832)
**Discovery of Cosette's letter and blotter**: Upon arrival at Rue de l'Homme Armé lodgings, Valjean found Cosette's blotting-book left open on sideboard in front of mirror. Book contained four lines of writing imprinted on blotter—a letter Cosette had written and given to young workman in Rue Plumet. Initially, examining blotter's reversed letters, Valjean saw no sense and experienced momentary relief. Then, looking in mirror, the four lines appeared with "inexorable clearness" in reflection—the reversal made them readable. **Valjean understood: Cosette had written to someone else.**

**Immediate collapse**: Valjean tottered, dropped blotter, fell into armchair beside buffet with drooping head and glassy eyes in utter bewilderment. Told himself light of world eclipsed forever; Cosette had written to someone. His soul gave vent to dull roar. **Core realization**: Cosette was escaping him, slipping from his hands like cloud and water; another was goal of her heart, wish of her life; he was no longer anything but her father, he no longer existed.

**Analysis of Valjean's paternal love**: Valjean loved Cosette as father only—yet into this paternity his life's widowhood introduced all shades of love: daughter, mother, sister, woman to love, wife. Never having known family love before, nature made him feel sentiment impossible to lose—vague, ignorant, pure with blindness's purity, unconscious, celestial, angelic, divine—like thread of gold in mountain, concealed and virgin. **Destinies were wedded though no marriage possible between them.**

**Philosophical crisis and spiritual collapse**: When confronted with absolute proof another was her dearest, Valjean felt grief surpassing bounds of possibility. Quiver of revolt ran through him head to foot; in very roots of hair, immense reawakening of egotism; the *I* in this man's abyss howled. **Inward subsoil gave way. Despairing certainty displaced and broke profound elements which were the very man himself—fatal crisis.** Valjean remained bowed, petrified, staring at four lines; cloud arose within him as though everything in his soul was crumbling.

**Recognition and divination**: He measured terrible step destiny had taken without suspicion; recalled fears of preceding summer, now foolishly dissipated; recognized the precipice—but was no longer on brink, at bottom. **Divination of despair struck Marius with first conjecture**—Valjean found the man instantly without knowing name. Perceived in background of memories the unknown prowler of Luxembourg, wretched seeker of love adventures, idler of romance, coward making eyes at young girl with devoted father. **After verification, Jean Valjean the regenerated man, who labored so over soul to resolve all life, misery, unhappiness into love, looked into own breast and beheld spectre: Hate.**

## Valjean's New Lodgings (Night of 24th June 1832)
**Location and refuge**: Rue de l'Homme Armé—narrow back alley of ancient Paris, barred against carriages, peaceable, dimly lit at midday, flanked by centuries-old silent houses, street of stagnant oblivion. **Lodgings situated on back court, second floor**: two sleeping-rooms, dining-room, kitchen adjoining, garret with folding-bed for Toussaint. Dining-room served as antechamber separating bedrooms. **Upon arrival, Valjean's anxiety lightened; soothing contagion of tranquility; thought: How could he be found there? Slept well. Next morning awoke in mood almost gay; found dining-room charming; ate wing of chicken with good appetite; gradually recovered serenity and regained sense of security.** **Twice or thrice noticed Toussaint stammering: "Monsieur, there is something going on, they are fighting in Paris"—but absorbed in calculations, paid no heed; had not heard.** Mental state before discovery: recovering serenity and sense of security, pacing door to window, growing ever more serene.

## Marius and Cosette's Romance (through evening 24th June 1832)
**Recognition, love, and garden encounters**: Upon reading Marius's manuscript, Cosette acknowledged she never forgot him, always loved him. Fire had smoldered, now burst forth afresh. Beginning autumn Year 5, Marius came every evening, entering by forcing old gate. At height of love's voluptuousness, Marius remained absolutely chaste. **Confessions of identity (spring Year 6, during cholera)**: Marius told Cosette—orphan, name Marius Pontmercy, lawyer, lived by writing, father colonel and hero, on bad terms with rich grandfather, hinted at being baron. Cosette told Marius—brought up at Petit-Picpus convent, mother dead, father M. Fauchelevent, very good, gave to poor.

**Éponine's death and letter (evening 24th June)**: **Éponine revealed she led Marius to barricade, stated**: "You are lost! You are going to die, I count upon that. When I saw them taking aim at you, I put my hand on the muzzle of the gun." Described memories of their encounters, spoke sweetly: "Everyone is going to die." Dropped head on Marius's knees; eyes closed, opened revealing death's sombre profundity; spoke in tone from another world. **Gave Marius letter from Cosette before dying.**

**Cosette's letter (discovered evening 24th June)**: Letter states marriage impossible; asked grandfather, refused; she has no fortune, neither has Marius; hastened to him, he no longer there; kept promise given; dies; loves him; when he reads, her soul will be near, he will smile. **Marius covered letter with kisses; reflected: She is going away, father taking her to England, grandfather refuses marriage. Nothing changed in fates. Resolved to fulfill two duties: inform Cosette of death and send farewell; save Gavroche from catastrophe.**

**Marius joins barricade (evening 24th June)**: Upon learning Valjean plans to take Cosette to England in one week, Marius declared gravest atrocity; protested lack of money; arranged to meet in garden 26th June at nine o'clock. **Same evening, approached grating, displaced bar, rushed in. Cosette not at waiting spot. Searched garden; deserted. Knocked repeatedly, called "Cosette!" No reply. Seated himself with heart filled with sweetness and resolution, blessed his love, said to himself since Cosette gone, all left was to die.** **Mad with grief, no longer conscious, incapable of accepting fate after two months intoxication, overwhelmed by reveries of despair, had one desire: speedy end.** Voice summoned him through twilight to barricade of Rue de la Chanvrerie. **Traversed boulevard, Esplanade, bridge of Invalides, Champs-Élysées, Place Louis XV, reached Rue de Rivoli, followed to Halles, reached Rue de la Poterie; received bullet wound near Rue du Contrat-Social; reached elbow of Rue Mondétour, perceived barricade interior at ten fathoms.** **Raised eyes; splendid rectification in mind. War of street transfigured by inward working of soul.** **Philosophy of duty**: Reflected on Colonel Pontmercy—proud soldier, guarded French frontier under Republic, touched Asia under Napoleon, beheld cities, left blood on battlefields, returned after twenty years with scarred cheek, smiling, pure as child. Own day had come; must follow father, show himself brave, run to meet bullets, offer breast to bayonets, shed blood, seek death. **Carries loaded pistols from time of 3d February adventure.** **During first phase**: Witnessed death of M. Mabeuf, Bahorel killed, Courfeyrac shouting; all hesitation vanished. **Flung himself into conflict, saved Gavroche with first shot, delivered Courfeyrac with second. Seized barrel of powder, took advantage of smoke to glide along barricade to cage of paving-stones where torch fixed, tore torch, replaced with barrel of powder, thrust pile of stones under it, staved in, stood with foot on stones, torch in hand, haughty face illuminated by fatal resolution, dropped flame toward redoubtable pile, gave vent to startling cry.** **Mental state**: Had furnace in brain all day; now whirlwind. Effect of being outside himself. Two luminous months of joy and love ending at frightful precipice, Cosette lost, barricade, M. Mabeuf killed for Republic, himself leader—all tremendous nightmare. Did not recognize Javert, bound to post.

## Barricade Details (Evening 24th June 1832)
**Café Corinthe**: Ground floor with bar; first floor with billiard-table and wooden spiral staircase; cellar accessible via trap-door; lodgings and attics. Proprietor: Widow Hucheloup. Serving-maids: Matelote (large, plump, red-haired), Gibelotte (tall, delicate, white, lymphatic).

**Two barricades constructed**: Enjolras, Combeferre, Courfeyrac directed. Larger shut off Rue de la Chanvrerie; other closed Rue Mondétour. Interior: irregular square, twenty paces between grand barrier and lofty houses. Issue left free on Rue Mondétour opening to Halles. **Larger barricade**: height six or seven feet, stepped construction, paling-stones, casks, wheels, omnibus pole with ropes, red flag. **Forty-three insurgents including Enjolras, Combeferre, Courfeyrac, Bossuet, Joly, Bahorel, Gavroche.** Six commanded by Feuilly at windows with guns levelled. Sentinels stationed.

**Javert's arrest**: Man of Rue des Billettes identified as Javert, Inspector of Police, aged fifty-two. Little round card identified him; also had watch, purse with gold pieces. Found paper in envelope—five lines in Prefect's handwriting, content not yet revealed.

**Le Cabuc execution**: Le Cabuc, utter stranger, examined house commanding whole street. **Enjolras, pale, Greek-profile, expression of wrath and chastity, executed him with pistol.** **Enjolras justified**: "Man killed, therefore I killed him. Insurrection must have discipline. I tried, condemned him, judged myself also." **Philosophy**: Necessity is monster of old world; progress shall eliminate it; love glorified; future: no one kills anyone else, earth beams with radiance. **Tradition**: Le Cabuc was Claquesous; left no trace, amalgamated himself with invisible.

**M. Mabeuf's heroic sacrifice**: Venerable old man of austerity. Had sold unique copy of Diogenes Laertius, returned with hundred francs, seated himself motionless at dawn. Evening 24th June: followed band, uttered no word, step became firm, refused arms, retreated into himself at Corinthe. **During attack**: At detonation, started up, crossed room, appeared on threshold as Enjolras appealed: "Does no one volunteer?" Tore flag from Enjolras. No one dared stop him. **Old man of eighty, shaking head but firm foot, began slowly ascending staircase of paving-stones. All cried: "Off with your hats!" White locks, decrepit face, aged arm upholding red banner rose through gloom, enlarged in bloody light.** **Enjolras's eulogy**: "This aged man teaches young. We hesitated, he came! This is magnificent death! Now defend this old man dead as his father living; his presence renders barricade impregnable!"

**Unknown figures**: Pale, thin, small, freckled, youthful artisan in tattered blouse and patched velvet trousers emerged from lodge, spoke to Courfeyrac in voice not in least womanly. **During attack**: soldier aimed at Marius; hand laid on muzzle, obstructed it. Done by young workman in velvet trousers. Shot traversed hand, possibly workman, who fell, but ball did not strike Marius.** Marius hardly noticed through smoke.

**After first assault**: Insurgents surprised but not terrified, rallied. Majority ascended to window on first story, commanded assailants. Some medical students cared for wounded. Thrown tables out of wine-shop except two for lint and cartridges, and one with Father Mabeuf; added to barricade; replaced with mattresses; wounded laid on them. Three poor creatures found hidden in cellar. **Assailants did not stir; could be heard marching through street but did not venture in.** Little barricade deserted, guarded only by fire-pot.
